card.name: Spots where a contrast is about to come
card.fires_on: Words and punctuation at the end of a clause that sets up a surprising or contrary point, such as 'might seem', 'anyway', 'still', 'yet' and a closing bracket or period after a concession. It appears in general web prose, not in drug-label text.

modes.label: Concession adverbs
modes.description: Adverbs like anyway, still, already or yet that signal something holds in spite of an obstacle.
modes.example: we will do so<< anyway>>. Keeping relative humidity in the 2

modes.label: Clause ends before a twist
modes.description: Verbs or punctuation that close a clause whose point is surprising against expectation.
modes.example: are not nearly as delicate as they might<< seem>>. Looking like dainty little fairies

modes.label: Parenthetical contrast
modes.description: A closing bracket after a qualifying aside that contrasts with the main claim.
modes.example: (though Muslims make up less than 2% of the U.S. population<<),>> reflecting a 142% increase

card.writes: It suppresses 'despite' and its translations, so it lowers the chance of a 'despite' phrase coming next.
card.plain: It marks the point in a sentence where a surprising or 'even so' idea has just been set up.
